auto_merge.commit_title: gh-140593: Fix a memory leak in function `my_ElementDeclHandler` of `pyexpat` (#140602)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Ensure that the memory allocated for the content model
passed to `my_ElementDeclHandler` is freed in all error
paths.

files.patch:
@@ -684,6 +684,23 @@ def test_change_size_2(self):
         parser.Parse(xml2, True)
         self.assertEqual(self.n, 4)
 
+class ElementDeclHandlerTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_trigger_leak(self):
+        # Unfixed, this test would leak the memory of the so-called
+        # "content model" in function ``my_ElementDeclHandler`` of pyexpat.
+        # See https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/140593.
+        data = textwrap.dedent('''\
+            <!DOCTYPE quotations SYSTEM "quotations.dtd" [
+                <!ELEMENT root ANY>
+            ]>
+            <root/>
+        ''').encode('UTF-8')
+
+        parser = expat.ParserCreate()
+        parser.NotStandaloneHandler = lambda: 1.234  # arbitrary float
+        parser.ElementDeclHandler = lambda _1, _2: None
+        self.assertRaises(TypeError, parser.Parse, data, True)
+
 class MalformedInputTest(unittest.TestCase):
     def test1(self):
         xml = b"\0\r\n"

@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+:mod:`xml.parsers.expat`: Fix a memory leak that could affect users with
+:meth:`~xml.parsers.expat.xmlparser.ElementDeclHandler` set to a custom
+element declaration handler. Patch by Sebastian Pipping.

review_comments.body:
I understand but there is a reason why I prefer inline calls like that:

- When no message is matched against, inline calls are better because they are more "oh this will just crash, it's just to check something).
- When there is a message to match against, it's important to know which part of the code actually did it. Sometimes it warrants a bit more comment, so a `with` block is usually betteer.

I also prefer having files that don't stretch vertically because it is harder to maintain them IMO. If you want to have an exact message to match, then the `with` block would be preferred.

Now, in this specific file, it seemed that the convention was to avoid `with` when possible for exceptions.

review_comments.body: @picnixz I don't really agree but thanks for elaborating.

issue_comments.body: How bad is it when the model is leaked? I see that you can leak only few bytes per bad call, so to cause a DoS you'll likely need many calls to blow-up the memory (and probably specific inputs) but I don't know which information is actually being leaked.
Sorry, job conditioning :) I meant "let's merge this once you've addressed the comments about the tests you added".

> How bad is it when the model is leaked? I see that you can leak only few bytes per bad call, so to cause a DoS you'll likely need many calls to blow-up the memory (and probably specific inputs)

@picnixz that is my impression too. So it's a bug but likely without attack surface.

> but I don't know which information is actually being leaked.

The so-called [content model](https://libexpat.github.io/doc/api/latest/#XML_SetElementDeclHandler). I adjusted in-test comments now realizing that the "32 to 56" bytes was due to the precise test and could be more depending on the input XML content.

> that is my impression too. So it's a bug but likely without attack surface.

Thanks. So I'll only backport this up to 3.13.

Thanks @hartwork for the PR, and @picnixz for merging it 🌮🎉.. I'm working now to backport this PR to: 3.13, 3.14.
